corrections.was: "He has been writing for an hour" is labelled present perfect.
corrections.now: That is present perfect continuous. Present perfect is has/have + past participle — "he has written". The row is left as the notes wrote it and flagged here; rewriting it would mean inventing an English and a Tamil sentence the notes do not contain.

corrections.was: "has been being", "had been being", "will have been being".
corrections.now: Not real English usage. Kept, because it is what the notes say and removing a row would hide the error rather than name it — the perfect continuous is has/have been + -ing.

corrections.was: may = fewer possibilities, might = more possibilities.
corrections.now: Reversed. "may" is the more likely of the two; "might" is the more tentative.

corrections.was: below example glossed "வெப்பநிலை சுழற்சி புள்ளியின் கீழே".
corrections.now: Corrected to "வெப்பநிலை பூஜ்ஜியத்திற்கு கீழே" — zero, not "cycle point".

corrections.was: the third column is headed "Conjunction", the same as the first.
corrections.now: It holds the English example sentence. Headed "English Example".

corrections.was: reflexives written as two words — "Him self", "Them selves-" — and "My" for the first person.
corrections.now: Myself, Ourselves, Yourself, Yourselves, Himself, Herself, Itself, Themselves.

corrections.was: each Example cell runs the pattern, the English sentence and the Tamil together with no separator — "Subject + Main Verb + ObjectI play cricketநான் cricket விளையாடுறேன்".
